newsitem.title: USA: Provident gets OK to buy First Citizens.
newsitem.headline: Provident gets OK to buy First Citizens.

text.p: Provident Bankshares Corp said Wednesday it received regulatory approval to buy First Citizens Financial Corp in a stock swap.

Provident will swap 2.75 million newly issued shares for First Citizens' stock in a 0.7665-for-one exchange ratio, said Provident's president and chief operating officer Pete Martin in an interview. Martin valued the deal, which the bank first announced March 11, at about $112 million.
"There will be a negligible dilution in the first year, but the acquistion will be accretive to earnings in the second year," Martin said. Provident now has 9.0 million shares outstanding.
The merger combines Provident's $3 billion assets and 49 branches with Citizens $700 million assets and 15 offices, Martin said.

"The real justification (for the take-over) is increased market share in Montgomery county, Md.," Martin said. He added the bank expects 30 percent in cost savings but plans to spend the savings on upgrading branch offices.
Stockholders of both companies will vote on the deal August 20, the company said. The bank expects to close the deal late August.
Provident's stock hit a 52-week high of 47-7/8 Wednesday, and was trading at 47-1/2 by mid-morning, up 1/4. First Citizens shares rose to 36-1/4, up 1-1/4.
